label: Plumbing
default_tone: practical and reassuring, with clear urgency for active leaks and no-water emergencies

content_slots.local_relevance: What drives plumbing problems varies a lot by region: in the Northeast and Midwest, winter freeze-thaw cycles crack pipes and cause bursts (water expands about 9% when it freezes); in the South and especially Texas, expansive clay soil shifts under slab foundations and is a major cause of slab leaks (over 95% of new homes in the West South Central states are built on concrete slabs); and hard-water regions see faster water heater failure and more drain clogs from mineral buildup.
content_slots.seasonal_calendar: Burst and frozen pipes spike in winter in cold-climate regions. Slab leaks and water heater failures are more evenly spread year-round but often surface after seasonal ground-shift (wet-to-dry cycles) in clay-soil regions. Drain clogs and water heater replacements are common in both spring and fall maintenance seasons.
